answer: Each agent identity dons a velvet cloak of staked capital: entry into the orchard of services requires burning an ember of stake, refundable only after a tenure of honest work. A sybil farmer gains extra shares by multiplying identities, but each clone risks its own stake to slashing on duplicated votes. Because losses scale faster than spam gains, the attacker's payoff turns negative once slash odds exceed fake-task profit. Equilibrium: one identity per unit of capital, and faking costs more than it yields.
